status: Conceptual figure content for an existing preliminary manuscript; no new evidence, counts or scope changes
authoring_scope: Local-source-only content audit and figure text. Rendering, numbering, manuscript integration and visual verification are separate tasks.

design_constraints.panel_fill: Equal card sizes; no inferred prevalence or evidence-strength encoding
design_constraints.reference_display: Keep full source IDs and PMIDs in this provenance file; captions carry a concise illustrative citation set already in the living bibliography.

figures.title: Separate evidence streams and their units of analysis
figures.suggested_layout: Three equal columns; a separate full-width clinical-background band below. Do not join the columns into a pooled estimate.

panels.label: A
panels.title: Patient care and access
lines: Units: patients, product records or interviews
Assess: need, costs, use and outcomes
Compare: recorded patient sex where measured
panels.boundary: One eligible population is not a between-sex comparison.

panels.label: B
panels.title: Service and anatomy valuation
panels.boundary: Anatomy and specialty do not measure physician gender.

panels.label: C
panels.title: Physician sex or gender
lines: Compare: measured physician sex or gender

supporting_band.title: Clinical and social background
supporting_band.text: Organizing frameworks support interpretation; they do not supply direct Medicare reimbursement estimates.

figures.footer: Preserve the measured variable, comparison axis and outcome. Do not infer patient disparities from clinician payments.
figures.caption: Three analytic streams answer different questions and require different units of analysis. Patient studies may compare recorded sex or describe care within one eligible population; neither recorded sex nor a diagnosis establishes gender identity. Service and anatomy studies compare procedures, resources or policies. Physician-gender studies compare clinicians and remain contextual to the patient-sex inquiry. Collections, salary and payment per service are distinct measures. Clinical reviews provide an organizing framework. Clinician interviews about patient barriers and prescriber datasets are classified by their analytic question, not by respondents' profession or data source. The diagram defines interpretation boundaries, not causal effects. [L-R01; L-P01; L-C03; L-Q01; L-B01; L-B01-E1]
interpretation_boundaries: The patient-care category contains population-specific and qualitative evidence; not every record supplies a male/female contrast.
Do not classify L-Q01 as physician-gender evidence or L-D01 as a clinician-pay comparison.
Do not pool physician-gender results with patient-sex or anatomy valuations.
The clinical background stream does not become an original Medicare reimbursement study.
No counts or directional results are encoded in panel size, color or arrangement.

figures.title: Classify the care indication separately from eligibility and burden
figures.figure_type: Conceptual clinical classification; no patient assignment or frequency encoding
figures.suggested_layout: Two rows of three equally sized category cards, then a separate band containing two independent descriptors. Retain all six original category names.

panels.label: A
panels.title: Shared systems or functions
lines: Examples: bone, breast, lymphatic and renal care
Compare within condition and clinical need

panels.label: D
panels.title: Female reproductive physiology
lines: Classify the indication, not the molecule

panels.label: F
panels.title: Mixed or site-dependent services
lines: Split diagnosis, site and procedure components

figures.footer: These categories describe care, not gender identity. Define clinical need independently of reimbursement rules.
figures.caption: Care-item classification concerns the recorded indication and anatomical or physiological target. Shared-system care may have unequal disease burden or sex-defined policy eligibility without becoming exclusive to one sex. Reproductive anatomy and reproductive physiology remain distinct: local vaginal treatment and systemic menopausal treatment illustrate this distinction. Mixed or site-dependent services require component-level review before comparison. Policy eligibility and population burden are separate descriptors, not additional anatomical categories. Clinical need is defined independently of reimbursement eligibility, and an opposite-sex counterpart is not required for every indication. These categories neither assign patient identity nor quantify national inequity. [L-B01; L-B01-E1; C-001; C-002; C-003; C-004]
interpretation_boundaries: Use the existing six categories without a new scope amendment or changes to active inventory.
Examples are from the existing classified indications; they are not statements that treatment is appropriate for every patient.
Do not infer gender identity from reproductive anatomy, diagnosis or medication.
Do not reclassify breast, bone, lymphatic, pelvic-floor or renal care as exclusive to women.
The broad prolapse row remains provisional until site and procedure verification.
Do not encode relative category size, national need or bias frequency.

figures.title: From financing measures to patient outcomes: links to test
figures.figure_type: Conceptual measurement pathway; dashed connections are hypotheses, not demonstrated causal effects
figures.suggested_layout: Three financing cards across the top feed, with dashed connectors, into an access card and then a health-outcome card. Place clinical need above all cards. Do not draw a serial coverage-to-payment-to-cost chain.

context_band.title: Clinical need and the eligible population
context_band.text: Assess indication, alternatives and preferences; retain people who never receive care.

panels.label: A
panels.title: Coverage and administration
panels.measurement_question: What does the dated policy permit?

panels.label: C
panels.title: Patient financial burden
panels.measurement_question: What does the patient actually bear?

panels.label: D
panels.title: Realized access
panels.measurement_question: Does indicated care reach the patient?

panels.label: E
panels.title: Health and patient experience
lines: Symptoms, function and quality of life

figures.edge_legend: Dashed links identify relationships requiring evaluation; direction and magnitude are unestablished.
figures.footer: Retain payer, policy year, age and entitlement. Compare equity in need, reach and outcomes separately.
figures.caption: Financing, access and patient outcomes are distinct measurement domains. The dashed links identify relationships to evaluate; they do not assert that coverage, higher payment or lower recorded spending causes better care. Policy permission differs from authorization performance, clinician receipts and patient out-of-pocket burden. Appropriate receipt, delays and unmet need require patient-level ascertainment, including people who do not complete a transaction. Health and experience outcomes require separate follow-up. Clinical need, indication, alternatives and preferences inform interpretation across the pathway. Analyses retain payer, policy period, age and entitlement, and evaluate equitable reach alongside average benefit. [L-D01; L-R01; L-P01; L-T01; L-T02]
interpretation_boundaries: The graph is a measurement framework, not a causal directed acyclic graph or a validated mediation model.
Dashed links must remain dashed and visibly labeled as hypotheses to test.
Do not imply that higher provider payment necessarily lowers patient cost or improves health.
Work RVUs, total RVUs, allowed payment and clinician receipts require separate estimands even within the payment panel.
Do not equate a submitted or approved request with receipt of appropriate care.
Average access improvement does not establish reduction in sex-related inequity.
Clinical eligibility must not be defined solely by benefit eligibility.

figures.title: Six health IT domains and their proposed evaluation targets
figures.figure_type: Unranked research-agenda matrix; targets are proposed outcomes, not observed product effects
figures.suggested_layout: Two columns by three rows. Each card contains domain name, one workflow line and one outcome line. Preserve O-IDs and an explicit unverified banner. No scoring, ranking or benefit-colored scale.
figures.status_banner: Unranked proposals. Clinical benefit, equitable reach and purchasing feasibility remain to be tested.

panels.label: O-01
panels.title: Medication affordability
lines: Measure: appropriate medication access and unmet need
panels.validation_design: Prospectively registered pragmatic cluster trial comparing existing RTBT/usual navigation with RTBT plus staffed closed-loop navigation; specify any cost-sharing assistance as a separate component.
panels.evidence_gap: No verified evidence that this proposed product closes a national patient-sex access gap. Incremental effectiveness after Part D redesign and cost-effectiveness remain unknown.

panels.label: O-02
panels.title: Post-fracture follow-up
lines: Test: registry plus accountable human follow-up
Measure: appropriate evaluation and shared decisions
panels.validation_design: Multisite pragmatic cluster trial of closed-loop follow-up versus existing discharge/referral processes, enrolling both sexes with clinically comparable qualifying fractures.
panels.evidence_gap: Digital incremental benefit, contemporary multi-payer effectiveness, fracture reduction and sex-specific benefit remain unestablished.

panels.label: O-03
panels.title: Non-drug authorization
lines: Measure: time to appropriate care and patient burden
panels.full_domain: Prior-authorization workflow for clinically indicated non-drug care
panels.validation_design: Prospective controlled rollout or cluster trial across defined services, with parallel clinically eligible patient ascertainment and audit of requests requiring manual handling.
panels.evidence_gap: No extracted study establishes this proposed product's patient benefit, cost-effectiveness or sex-gap closure. National administrative metrics do not supply a patient-level causal test.

panels.label: O-04
panels.title: Procedure-valuation research
lines: Test: transparent comparator and resource audit
panels.validation_design: Registered multicenter measurement study with independently adjudicated comparators, full-episode work sampling and external replication; only subsequently evaluate downstream policy changes using a justified causal design.
panels.evidence_gap: The three headline contrasts are not directly poolable; contemporary full-resource measurements and causal downstream access effects are missing.

panels.label: O-05
panels.title: Lymphedema item fulfillment
lines: Measure: timely receipt, fit and ability to use
panels.validation_design: Prospective post-2024 access audit followed by a controlled or randomized fulfillment intervention across diverse suppliers and clinical sites.
panels.evidence_gap: Current national fulfillment, fit and cost-sharing barriers after the benefit expansion have not been established by the cited studies.

panels.label: O-06
panels.title: Kidney-care coordination
lines: Test: human-led education and practical support
panels.full_domain: Kidney-care education and practical support coordination
panels.validation_design: Begin with US Medicare patient/caregiver interviews and an access audit, then co-design and pilot a controlled coordination intervention before a definitive pragmatic trial.
panels.evidence_gap: No directly evaluated Medicare technology intervention or verified patient-sex benefit in the cited record. Patient and caregiver evidence is required before product selection.

figures.footer: For every domain: compare existing services; measure harms, burden and equitable reach; verify implementation and buyer need.
figures.caption: Six purposively selected domains translate the local evidence register into prospective evaluation questions. The workflow and outcome in each panel are proposals, not established effects of a digital product. Medication and fracture-care interventions provide precedents for testing specified approaches; effectiveness does not automatically transfer to other domains. Procedure valuation initially requires reliable research measurements, with patient effects assessed separately. All proposals require comparison with existing services, clinically appropriate denominators, harms monitoring and explicit equity assessment. Coverage or an interoperability requirement does not establish software reimbursement, customer demand or profitability. Domain order conveys no priority or ranking. [L-T01; L-T02; L-G05; L-P01; L-P02; L-A02; L-Q01; P-054]
interpretation_boundaries: These are the six existing unranked opportunity domains, not a census, new recommendations or verified markets.
O-04 is research infrastructure with indirect patient benefit; do not depict it as an effective treatment or access intervention.
O-02 evaluation/shared decisions are not synonymous with fracture prevention.
O-03 is the existing non-drug proposal; do not depict proposed drug-authorization rules as effective policy.
O-05 historical cost/coverage studies do not establish present post-benefit fulfillment barriers.
O-06 international clinician perceptions do not establish US Medicare patient barrier prevalence or a measured patient-sex effect.
Keep patient benefits, process measures, equity and purchasing feasibility distinct.
Do not imply that all six domains have randomized evidence or comparable evidence maturity.
